title: Woman claims her stepfather used Grok to transform childhood photo into explicit imagery
slides: Can AI turn innocent photos into explicit ones?
This woman says her stepfather did exactly that.
Grok's image editor allegedly enabled the abuse.
Another app's limits: what is legally actionable now?
Review your family photos and AI platform policies today.
thread_text:
1. She caught him red-handed

Her stepfather allegedly used Grok's image editor to turn innocent family photos into explicit ones — and she found the evidence on his phone.

2. The tool's defense

Grok's maker says the feature wasn't designed for abuse, but the platform has no real age verification or photo-consent check before edits are made.

3. What the law can't touch

Most states only criminalize creating explicit images of minors, not adults. So if the victim is over 18, the abuser may face no charges at all.

4. The gap in every app

Other AI editors have similar loopholes — they refuse to make child porn, but will happily alter an adult photo without proof of consent from the person in it.

5. Audit your phone tonight

Review your family photos and the AI policies on every app you use. If you find an altered image, report it — but know that legal protection may not exist yet.
